title: Rounding Worksheets to the Nearest 10 and 100
intro: Teach rounding by comparing distances to neighboring multiples.
html:
Teaching notes for parents and teachers

How to teach it

Place the number between consecutive tens or hundreds on a number line. Locate the midpoint before using a digit rule.

Example to work through together

Use the model below as you explain the example. Have your student point to the quantities as you discuss them.

Nearest ten: 347 is between 340 and 350; choose 350.

Nearest hundred: 347 is between 300 and 400; choose 300.

Ask your student

Which endpoint is closer to this number?

If your student needs help

If the student rounds to the wrong place, have them name the two possible rounded values first.

Choosing and using the worksheet

Each set contains six distinct number-and-place questions from the original bank. Numbers range from 10 through 989, with requests for the nearest 10 or 100. The key gives the rounded value. Write neighboring multiples or a short distance comparison in the working space.
